architectureDecisions: D1 — Current source truth: Backend and QA call packages/agentic-system/src/oracle.js before Worker execution, so Oracle IO is still physically Application-owned.
D2 — Core already owns bounded context selection/renderAgentContext; dynamic context blocks are projection, not durable source-resolution identity/currentness.
D3 — Capability, Resource and LiveObject are not the default Oracle seam; required grounding must not become model/tool-call behavior.

D4 — Target path: Application semantic need -> ContextRequirement -> Core pre-prompt injected resolver -> Oracle -> providers/planner -> ContextResolution -> existing Core context projection. BB-061 owns the production contract.
D5 — Core consumes the resolver by dependency injection; Core does not import Oracle implementation and Oracle imports neither Core nor Agentic Application.
D6 — BB-060 adds no production Core resolver hook or temporary ContextRequirement/ContextResolution API; BB-061 owns both.
D7 — Create private @exharness/oracle and move source loops into readRepositorySources() and readApplicationArtifacts() provider modules with injected readers and source provenance only.
D8 — Keep packages/agentic-system/src/oracle.js as compatibility adapter preserving resolveBackendContext/resolveQaContext and existing Application schema validation.
D9 — BB-060 providers are concrete building blocks, not a provider registry/planner/lifecycle system; BB-062 selects provider topology after experiments.
D10 — Development-only runtime seam probe resolves outside model-visible tools, projects the result into an ordinary Core context block, then calls renderAgentContext.
D11 — Architecture guards reject Oracle->agentic/core imports, Core->Oracle implementation imports, copied source loops and Oracle lifecycle/acceptance authority.

D12 — Evidence patterns: Aider=budgeted structural projection, Serena/SolidLSP=semantic symbols, Zoekt=lexical baseline, Graphiti/Cognee=context-graph candidates, Uber=context-infrastructure evidence. BB-060 selects no backend.
D13 — Serena application is GPL-3.0-or-later while SolidLSP is MIT; full Serena is not selected by BB-060.
D14 — Living Docs describe only delivered physical/provider compatibility; production ContextRequirement/ContextResolution remains NOT YET DELIVERED until BB-061.
D15 — Preserve no-install CI: declare file:../oracle metadata but use ../../oracle/src/index.js source import; no CI workflow or lockfile change.
implementationSlices: S1 [PHYSICAL_OWNERSHIP,COMPATIBILITY] — Create packages/oracle/package.json exactly as private ESM package @exharness/oracle@0.1.0 exporting ./src/index.js. index.js exports only readRepositorySources and readApplicationArtifacts. repository-source.js implements readRepositorySources({repositoryRef,revision,requiredFiles},{repositoryReader}) -> {repository:{ref:repositoryRef,revision},files:[{path,content,sourceRef}]}. application-artifact-source.js implements readApplicationArtifacts({requiredArtifacts,producerWorkOrderId,revision,acceptanceDecision},{artifactReader}) -> {artifacts:[{ref,path?,content,sourceRef,provenance:{sourceClass:'APPLICATION_ARTIFACT',producerWorkOrderId,acceptanceDecision}}]}. Both own the concrete read loops, validate injected reader methods, fail closed on missing/invalid read results, and import no Core/Agentic Application module.

S2 [COMPATIBILITY] — packages/agentic-system/src/oracle.js keeps only resolveBackendContext(rawOrder,{repositoryReader}) and resolveQaContext(rawOrder,{artifactReader}) compatibility orchestration. Backend: parseBackendWorkOrder -> readRepositorySources -> BackendContextSchema.parse. QA: parseQaWorkOrder -> readApplicationArtifacts -> QaContextSchema.parse({upstream,artifacts,acceptanceCriteria}). The adapter performs no repositoryReader.readFile/artifactReader.readArtifact loop; tests require the same reader call arguments/order, sourceRef and APPLICATION_ARTIFACT provenance, and causal fail-closed errors.

S3 [PHYSICAL_OWNERSHIP] — packages/agentic-system/package.json adds dependencies.@exharness/oracle='file:../oracle'; source uses ../../oracle/src/index.js because CI does not run npm install. Root package.json adds test:oracle='node --test packages/oracle/test/*.test.js test/oracle-context-intelligence-architecture.test.mjs' and appends npm run test:oracle to test. Do not add package-lock or modify .github workflows. packages/oracle/test/compatibility-providers.test.js covers success, missing reader, reader rejection and malformed result; packages/agentic-system/test/oracle-package-integration.test.js covers both unchanged application adapters.

S4 [PHYSICAL_OWNERSHIP,REBOUND_SEMANTICS,INV-1,INV-3] — test/oracle-context-intelligence-architecture.test.mjs mechanically checks: Oracle source imports contain no agentic-system/core path; core-harness source/package contains no @exharness/oracle or packages/oracle implementation import; agentic-system/src/oracle.js contains no '.readFile(' or '.readArtifact('; agentic-system declares file:../oracle; Oracle exports are exactly the two S1 provider functions. In-memory mutated-text fixtures must make each forbidden import/read-loop/export case fail.

S5 [RUNTIME_PATH,PROTOTYPE_HANDOFF,INV-2] — scripts/oracle-context-intelligence/bb060-runtime-seam-probe.mjs uses deterministic fixtures only: semanticNeed -> injected resolver function -> readRepositorySources -> define one ordinary required Core context block from returned source/provenance -> renderAgentContext. It never calls AgentRuntime.invoke/Capability/Resource/LiveObject. Exit nonzero unless providerCalls=1, actionCalls=0, exact sourceRef/provenance survives, renderedChars<=declared maxSerializedChars, and provider failure yields no rendered prompt. On success print one JSON record with providerCalls,actionCalls,sourceReads,materializedChars,renderedChars,provenanceCoverage,wallMs,failureClass for later benchmark ingestion.

S6 [REBOUND_SEMANTICS] — Update docs/living/system/oracle/{architecture,state,semantics,workflow}.md with only delivered @exharness/oracle provider ownership, compatibility path and limitations. State verbatim that production ContextRequirement/ContextResolution and the Core pre-prompt resolver hook are NOT YET DELIVERED and belong to BB-061; do not claim graph/search/planner delivery.

S7 [EXIT] — Execute in order: node --test packages/oracle/test/compatibility-providers.test.js; node --test packages/agentic-system/test/oracle-package-integration.test.js packages/agentic-system/test/wave-a.test.js packages/agentic-system/test/wave-c.test.js packages/agentic-system/test/bb043-artifact-manifest-adapter.test.js; node --test test/oracle-context-intelligence-architecture.test.mjs; node scripts/oracle-context-intelligence/bb060-runtime-seam-probe.mjs; npm run test:agentic; npm test. Worker output is limited to the files in sourceScope.write and evidence for the declared acceptance criteria; any need for a production Core hook, provider registry/planner or backend selection returns to research instead of expanding BB-060.
